title: CE5 verification-method amendment: OpenTimestamps proof verification without a local Bitcoin node

amends.requirement_replaced: OpenTimestamps proof at <--prereg file>.ots commits to this file and carries a Bitcoin attestation, and a successful ots verify run is recorded at <--prereg file>.ots.verification.json
amends.replaced_by: an amendment-01 Java OpenTimestamps record at <--prereg file>.ots.java_explorer_corroboration.json that design.java_ots_verification_ok accepts

reason: No local Bitcoin node is available, so the registered 'ots verify' record cannot be produced; the registered gate refuses production (gate_before_amendment.json).
unchanged: the design (hash 409e7dcb53c5eba7a623a584ec302f2aa3a26e84b3efcf9e6c021e5629fde5c5) and every statistical rule
the approved preregistration file and its upgraded proof (bytes and hashes above)
every other production check: approval, confirm token, proof digest, Bitcoin attestation, design equals design.py, source integrity, table validation, memory, checkpoint binding
the registered gate path: without --amendment, production still requires the ots verify record

method.name: Java OpenTimestamps explorer-assisted verification plus independent second-endpoint raw-header corroboration
procedure: run the pinned Java CLI: java -jar OtsCli.jar -v verify -f <prereg> <prereg>.ots (runner stage 'javaots'); with no bitcoin.conf it looks up each attested block at the Java endpoint
fetch /block-height/<h> and /block/<hash>/header for every Bitcoin attestation from the second endpoint
record all of it raw (runner.record_java_ots_verification); the recorder judges nothing

the gate (design.java_ots_verification_ok) recomputes from the record and the proof: proof operation tree evaluated from the file digest to each attested Merkle root; Java success line for the earliest height, exit code 0 and no failure output; Java endpoint block hash and Merkle root per height; second-endpoint header is 80 bytes, double-SHA-256 equals the same block hash, Merkle root equals the commitment, time equals the Java endpoint's
is_not: local Bitcoin Core consensus verification: no node validates the chain or the headers' proof of work against it; block validity is taken from two public explorers

a two-endpoint implementation inside the Java CLI: java-opentimestamps 8186391 (upstream HEAD on 2026-11-08) queries one Esplora endpoint (https://blockstream.info/api); its README still describes a two-endpoint rule whose code (MultiInsight) was removed in commit 91407bb (2020-04-26). The second endpoint is queried and checked by CE5 code, not by the Java CLI
method.java_exit_code_caveat: the Java CLI catches verification exceptions and exits 0 (phase_a_java_negative_wrong_file); exit code 0 is required but never sufficient

compatibility_demonstration.result: Java CLI: 'Success! Bitcoin block 974769'; blocks 974769 and 974770 looked up at the Java endpoint; second-endpoint raw headers hash to the same block hashes and carry the proof's Merkle roots
